pr_title: Accept new Plex websocket callback payloads
pr_body:
<!--

## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
Relies on changes in library: https://github.com/jjlawren/python-plexwebsocket/compare/v0.0.11...v0.0.12

Accepts new payloads in callbacks provided by websocket library. Allows to differentiate between connection status changes, receive the actual payload data, and know which errors may have occurred.

If an error occurs in the websocket connection the integration will reload itself and rely on the standard config flow setup fallback mechanism. Transient errors are still handled in the library, so this should be a rare event.

To go along with this reload, the logging is reduced on initial connection failures as the core logging is sufficient.

Hopefully addresses setups with not-always-up Plex servers: https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/39979.

would hope to be able to do something like this:
```
automation:
  - alias: Plex host offline
    trigger:
      platform: state
      entity_id: binary_sensor.plex_host_ping
      to: 'off'
      for:
        minutes: 2
    condition: []
    action:
      - service: stop polling Plex server #<-- new service
      - service: notify.notify
        data_template:
          title: Plex server offline
          message: >
            {{as_timestamp(now())|timestamp_custom('%X')}} :
            {{trigger.to_state.name}} has gone is {{trigger.to_state.state}}-line.
            Check status to restore functionality. We wont poll any further until
            {{trigger.to_state.name}} is back online again. To keep the log from flooding ;-)

  - alias: Plex host online
    trigger:
      platform: state
      entity_id: binary_sensor.plex_host_ping
      to: 'on'
      from: 'off'
    condition: []
    action:
      - service: start polling Plex server #<-- new service
      - service: notify.notify
        data_template:
          title: Plex server offline
          message: >
            {{as_timestamp(now())|timestamp_custom('%X')}} :
            {{trigger.to_state.name}} has gone back {{trigger.to_state.state}}-line.
```

which would only require the ping binary_sensor.
comments:
Hey there @jjlawren, mind taking a look at this issue as its been labeled with an integration (`plex`) you are listed as a [codeowner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L327) for? Thanks!
<sub><sup>(message by CodeOwnersMention)</sup></sub>
When HA is started when the Plex server is unavailable, it should detect this and recover once it comes online (with some delay). Is this not working for you?

well, apparently not...
check the log snippets I posted. the integration causes huge log spam

do you know of any setting I could change to mitigate this? Seems the integration simply keeps trying to logon, while the server is offline

It should handle the Plex server unavailable at startup and should recover when it becomes available using a backoff mechanism. Are you certain it doesn't recover automatically?

Here's an example from my environment:
```
2020-09-15 14:50:22 WARNING (MainThread) [homeassistant.config_entries] Config entry for plex not ready yet. Retrying in 5 seconds
2020-09-15 14:50:27 ERROR (MainThread) [homeassistant.components.plex] Plex server (https://10-0-10-80.123456.plex.direct:32400) could not be reached: [HTTPSConnectionPool(host='10-0-10-80.123456.plex.direct', port=32400): Max retries exceeded with url: / (Caused by NewConnectionError('<urllib3.connection.HTTPSConnection object at 0x7fb355f088d0>: Failed to establish a new connection: [Errno 111] Connection refused'))]
2020-09-15 14:50:27 WARNING (MainThread) [homeassistant.config_entries] Config entry for plex not ready yet. Retrying in 10 seconds
2020-09-15 14:50:37 ERROR (MainThread) [homeassistant.components.plex] Plex server (https://10-0-10-80.123456.plex.direct:32400) could not be reached: [HTTPSConnectionPool(host='10-0-10-80.123456.plex.direct', port=32400): Max retries exceeded with url: / (Caused by NewConnectionError('<urllib3.connection.HTTPSConnection object at 0x7fb355c05d90>: Failed to establish a new connection: [Errno 111] Connection refused'))]
2020-09-15 14:50:37 WARNING (MainThread) [homeassistant.config_entries] Config entry for plex not ready yet. Retrying in 20 seconds
```
If the Plex server is disabled during runtime there are currently no specific checks to throttle reconnections as it assumes the downtime is transient.

Assuming it does recover by itself, do you have any issues besides the "noise" in the logs?

first off, these were 2 different issues.
- starting up Ha when a Plex server is offline
- turning off a Plex server when Ha is online

and about the downtime being transient, that might be something else than a planned downtime during nighttime? I guess a dip in power or short outage could be mitigated with this, but that would indeed be as short as possible hopefully. We're talking 8 hours here, with only Plex littering (sorry, noising) the log... 

Maybe the error level could be changed, but it would be better if another way of checking the up/downstatus could be implemented.

It's understood there are two reported issues. I believe the first issue ("starting up Ha when a Plex server is offline") should _not_ be behaving the way you're describing. It if is, I'll need more information as your logs don't indicate problems at startup.

The request to change how the integration reports errors when the Plex server is unavailable is acknowledged. To confirm, is your primary complaint that the logging is excessive? Or does it cause other functional issues?

posted a reply to this but apparently my device didnt get through...

I dont have much more to go on, other than the error doesnt slow down, and does keep logging every 1.5-2 minutes or so, as was seen in the log snippet. I realize setting log level in logger wouldn relieve me of the heavy spamming, but might also cause necessary errors to be missed? Not sure.

I don't think other functional issues arise. I must check if the Plex sensors are in fact being created when HA starts up with the Plex server down or that they, like the Synology sensors, show the yellow bar in Lovelace (instead of showing unavailable), which is a true bug imho. other integration :-)

Are you not seeing any of these errors in your logs?

Are you able to share logs from when the problem first begins after shutting down your Plex server / NAS?

review_comments: Will the callback be run in async context or sync context? Here we use the async api but above we also use  `asyncio.run_coroutine_threadsafe` which hints at it running in sync context.
You're right. The callback is always called from an async context. Will review and polish the other call in a followup.
If we don't need to wait for the result we can use `hass.add_job`.
Change to if-else to avoid evaluate all if statements if the prior one is true
